sections.overview: Euproctis similis, the Yellow-tail, is a tussock moth in the family Erebidae; its French common name is Cul-doré.
sections.identification: The adult has a 28–35 mm wingspan; females are larger and carry a conspicuous yellow hair tuft at the abdomen tip.
sections.habitat: Its caterpillars feed on deciduous trees and shrubs, with French field records including willow and poplar.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on deciduous woody plants; sources list several trees and shrubs rather than one exclusive host.
sections.behavior: Larvae bear irritating hairs and should not be handled; the female uses her yellow abdominal tuft to cover newly laid eggs.
sections.reproduction: It has one generation each year and overwinters as a solitary third-instar larva. Pupation occurs in foliage.
sections.ecology: It resembles the Brown-tail, Euproctis chrysorrhoea, and has a similar life cycle, but its larvae are solitary rather than gregarious; see that related profile.
sections.conservation: The consulted regional accounts document its occurrence but do not provide a current global conservation assessment.
